source: National Archives Amendments 11–27 transcript, Amendment XXIV Section 1
review_notes: Codex reviewed the complete clause. Six election offices or elector roles, two government actors, denial and abridgment, and poll or other tax grounds are each represented. The any-primary-or-other-election quantifier remains in every condition, rather than being mistaken for a single named election. The positive voting rights are also recorded. These are Codex labels, not independent human labels.
text:
AMENDMENT XXIV
Section 1.
The right of citizens of the United States to vote in any primary or other election for President or Vice President, for electors for President or Vice President, or for Senator or Representative in Congress, shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or any State by reason of failure to pay any poll tax or other tax.
